candidates.draft_title: Fix coach search filters resetting on browser back navigation
candidates.snippet:
[EXTERNAL] Aisha Bramble: So. People are complaining about finding a coach. Not that there aren't coaches — there are — but the search itself is annoying them.
[EXTERNAL] Aisha Bramble: Okay so you go to the coach search, and there are filters, right? Specialty, language, timezone, all that.
[EXTERNAL] Aisha Bramble: So our folks set up their filters carefully. Say someone wants a coach who speaks Spanish, does reactive-dog rehabilitation, in their timezone. They tick all three, get a nice list.
[EXTERNAL] Aisha Bramble: Then they click into a coach's profile to read the bio. And then they hit the browser back button to go back to the list — and all their filters are gone. Wiped. Back to square one.
[EXTERNAL] Aisha Bramble: Exactly. Every single filter, cleared. So they're staring at the full unfiltered list again and have to re-tick Spanish, leadership, timezone, all of it, from scratch.
[EXTERNAL] Aisha Bramble: The browser back button, yeah. The top-left arrow. That's what everyone instinctively hits after reading a profile. And boom, selections lost.
[EXTERNAL] Aisha Bramble: You've got it. And when you're comparing four or five coaches, you're re-entering those filters four or five times. People are giving up before they book.
[EXTERNAL] Aisha Bramble: Anecdotally yes. Two people literally told me "I couldn't be bothered, the search kept resetting." Which for a coaching program is a bad reason to not get coached.
[EXTERNAL] Aisha Bramble: That's it exactly. The selections don't survive the back navigation.
[EXTERNAL] Aisha Bramble: We're a Chrome shop almost entirely, so I can only confirm Chrome. I haven't heard about others because nobody here uses others.
[EXTERNAL] Aisha Bramble: Please do. It's not a crash or anything dramatic, it's just death by a thousand re-clicks.
[EXTERNAL] Aisha Bramble: Feel free. I workshop my complaints, I'm a media person.
[EXTERNAL] Aisha Bramble: The one clever guy opens each coach profile in a new tab instead of clicking through. Then the list tab keeps its filters. But nobody thinks to do that naturally.
[EXTERNAL] Aisha Bramble: Agreed. The tab trick is a band-aid. The real fix is the filters not evaporating.
